ownership.concern: tokens, theme, density, responsive regimes, layers
basic structure, text, shared pressable semantics
page geometry, safe areas, adaptive composition
navigation surfaces and Expo Router boundary
fields, sections, validation presentation, keyboard shell
locale, messages, fallback, formatting, direction, pseudo-localization
loading, empty, error, offline, retry, stale feedback
runtime providers, services, isolated async actions
query identity, scoped cache, stale refresh, invalidation, and mutation lifecycle
selected native/browser capability adapters and availability
provider-neutral logging, error reporting, analytics timing

items.purpose: Own page bounds, scrolling, safe-area behavior, form keyboard handling, and content width.
items.useWhen: Starting any route or full-screen product surface.
items.doNotUseWhen: A dialog, bottom sheet, or list already owns scrolling.
items.responsiveBehavior: Uses shared content widths and responsive regimes; routes do not calculate widths.
items.accessibility: Provides a consistent screen/scroll boundary; pair with semantic headings.
items.platformNotes: FormScreen owns the native keyboard-controller boundary.

items.purpose: Create semantic page hierarchy and action composition without route-owned spacing.
items.useWhen: A page needs a title, metadata, section grouping, or page-level actions.
items.doNotUseWhen: A Golden pattern already supplies the same header/section anatomy.
items.responsiveBehavior: Headers and actions recompose across compact and expanded regimes.
items.accessibility: SectionHeader and heading primitives preserve hierarchy.
items.platformNotes: Portable across native and web.

items.purpose: Own compact/medium/expanded/wide recomposition.
items.useWhen: A product surface changes structure across shared responsive regimes.
items.doNotUseWhen: The distinction is only content; keep one semantic composition instead.
items.responsiveBehavior: Uses tokenized breakpoints rather than feature viewport branches.
items.accessibility: Preserves a single mounted content path across regimes.
items.platformNotes: Do not call useWindowDimensions or Platform.OS in feature routes.

items.purpose: Compose a settings/account form with sanctioned page, field, and action anatomy.
items.useWhen: Editing product preferences, account settings, or a small grouped form.
items.doNotUseWhen: The workflow is multi-step; start with WizardLayout instead.
items.responsiveBehavior: Form actions stack safely on compact layouts.
items.accessibility: Use visible labels, descriptions, field errors, and first-invalid focus through form-RHF when needed.
items.platformNotes: FormScreen owns keyboard avoidance; do not add KeyboardAvoidingView.

items.purpose: Compose searchable, filterable, sortable, selectable data workspaces.
items.useWhen: Displaying an ordinary controlled dataset with filters, row actions, or bulk actions.
items.doNotUseWhen: The dataset needs very large table virtualization; remote data should be supplied through @precision-calm/server-state without moving cache ownership into the table.
items.responsiveBehavior: Table transforms to structured compact records below expanded layouts.
items.accessibility: Selection, toolbar, and row controls expose shared semantics.
items.platformNotes: Pair remote rows with @precision-calm/server-state; keep transport/query ownership outside the table.

items.purpose: Compose result screens with a shared list/state hierarchy.
items.useWhen: Search results, browse pages, or a result list with a domain-owned query input.
items.doNotUseWhen: A dense workspace/table is the primary content; use DataWorkspaceLayout.
items.responsiveBehavior: Uses shared page and list geometry.
items.accessibility: Use named search controls and shared state announcements.
items.platformNotes: Pair the pattern with @precision-calm/server-state for remote data.

items.purpose: Compose overview pages with metrics, primary work, and contextual panels.
items.useWhen: Starting a dashboard or operational home route.
items.doNotUseWhen: The page is primarily a table, feed, detail, or form.
items.responsiveBehavior: Primary and secondary content use pattern-owned adaptive slots.
items.accessibility: Metrics retain label/value relationships.
items.platformNotes: Included in the generated home route.

items.purpose: Own labelled text entry, descriptions, errors, disabled/read-only behavior, and input intent.
items.useWhen: Collecting the currently supported text/password/search/currency input.
items.doNotUseWhen: A product needs searchable choice, date/time/range, OTP, or file/media input; use the corresponding specialized Golden owner.
items.responsiveBehavior: Uses shared field metrics and bounded labels.
items.accessibility: Visible label and description/error relationships are owned by the field.
items.platformNotes: Never use raw TextInput in a feature route.

items.purpose: Own current choice controls and their anchored overlay/selection semantics.
items.useWhen: Selecting static options or a boolean value.
items.doNotUseWhen: The product needs autocomplete, multi-select, grouped checkbox errors, or segmented selection.
items.responsiveBehavior: Select presentation uses shared popover/menu geometry.
items.accessibility: Choice controls own checked/selected semantics.
items.platformNotes: Never use raw Switch in a feature route.

items.purpose: Own consistent form grouping, descriptions, errors, action order, and responsive composition.
items.useWhen: A form has multiple fields, sections, help text, or submission actions.
items.doNotUseWhen: A one-control action is already fully represented by its component.
items.responsiveBehavior: Actions stack in compact layouts.
items.accessibility: Preserves field labels, help, and error context.
items.platformNotes: Use with FormScreen for native keyboard ownership.

items.canonicalName: usePrecisionForm, controlled field adapters, keyboard flow, error focus
items.purpose: Provide optional React Hook Form wiring, blur validation, keyboard Next/Done, first-invalid focus, and shared form-lifecycle integration.
items.useWhen: A product has chosen React Hook Form for an existing supported field flow.
items.doNotUseWhen: Creating a form state abstraction or importing react-hook-form directly in a route.
items.responsiveBehavior: Delegates geometry to forms/layouts.
items.accessibility: Focuses the first invalid supported field.
items.platformNotes: Optional integration; drafts, autosave, arrays, and dependent fields remain later work.

items.purpose: Own post-submit error summary, server-error mapping through form-RHF, dirty-state leave confirmation, and reset lifecycle.
items.useWhen: A supported form needs server validation feedback, a focusable error summary, reset, or unsaved-change protection.
items.doNotUseWhen: Persisting drafts, building offline autosave, or inventing a route-specific navigation guard; those require later server-state or optional storage boundaries.
items.responsiveBehavior: Summary actions and discard actions stack safely on compact layouts.
items.accessibility: One alert summary links to registered invalid fields; inline field errors remain polite and contextual.
items.platformNotes: Use FormScreen for keyboard ownership and the optional form-RHF lifecycle adapter for React Hook Form.

items.purpose: Connect supported React Hook Form flows to the shared post-submit summary, server-error mapping, reset, and dirty-leave lifecycle.
items.useWhen: A product has chosen React Hook Form and needs the supported shared form lifecycle.
items.doNotUseWhen: Persisting drafts, implementing autosave, arrays, or dependent-field orchestration; those remain later capabilities.
items.responsiveBehavior: Delegates layout and keyboard behavior to forms and FormScreen.
items.accessibility: Maps one post-submit summary to registered field focus while retaining contextual inline errors.
items.platformNotes: Optional RHF integration; feature routes must not import react-hook-form directly.

items.purpose: Own locale normalization, message fallback, plural selection, formatting, direction, pseudo-localization, and RTL-safe icon/layout behavior.
items.useWhen: Displaying product copy through message IDs, formatting values, sorting user-visible strings, or responding to locale direction.
items.doNotUseWhen: Adding a translation vendor, provider-specific translation workflow, or product catalog to the shared kernel.
items.responsiveBehavior: Direction is applied at the runtime root; shared owners use semantic start/end and recomposition rules.
items.accessibility: Sets web document language/direction and preserves semantic directional icons without changing accessible names.
items.platformNotes: Uses built-in Intl only; no translation or native locale dependency is installed by the kernel.

items.purpose: Own loading, empty, no-results, error, offline, reconnect, permission, maintenance, retry, and stale/degraded presentation.
items.useWhen: A route or section has product-owned asynchronous state and needs standard feedback anatomy.
items.doNotUseWhen: A bare action is loading; use Button loading or LoadingState instead.
items.responsiveBehavior: Uses bounded shared feedback layout.
items.accessibility: Shared messages and actions provide consistent semantics.
items.platformNotes: Map @precision-calm/server-state query lifecycle with toPrecisionAsyncState; presentation remains separate from transport.

items.purpose: Show transient loading and inline outcome feedback without raw spinners.
items.useWhen: Loading a page, list, card, or presenting a compact non-blocking message.
items.doNotUseWhen: The state needs a full empty/error/retry action; use StateView or AsyncStateView.
items.responsiveBehavior: Uses shared sizing and density metrics.
items.accessibility: Labels supply announcement context.
items.platformNotes: Never use raw ActivityIndicator in feature routes.

items.purpose: Present a focused confirmation or destructive decision through the shared overlay root.
items.useWhen: Confirming a consequential or destructive product action.
items.doNotUseWhen: Choosing from a small action list; use ActionMenu or Menu.
items.responsiveBehavior: Uses overlay-owned modal geometry and layer order.
items.accessibility: Modal role, initial focus, keyboard focus trap, Escape policy, and safe restoration are shared.
items.platformNotes: Never use raw Modal or a feature-owned backdrop.

items.purpose: Present contextual workflow content with overlay-owned scrolling, keyboard dismissal, and safe sizing.
items.useWhen: A mobile-friendly contextual workflow or long overlay is appropriate.
items.doNotUseWhen: A full route or destructive confirmation provides clearer navigation semantics.
items.responsiveBehavior: Uses sheet-specific compact and desktop max-width rules.
items.accessibility: Modal role, initial focus, keyboard focus trap, Escape policy, long-content scrolling, and safe restoration are shared.
items.platformNotes: Do not create fixed feature bars or raw modal sheets.

items.purpose: Own anchored placement, measurement, dismissal, and action-menu semantics.
items.useWhen: Offering contextual actions or a small anchored menu.
items.doNotUseWhen: The option requires searchable/autocomplete input; that control is not current.
items.responsiveBehavior: Popover collision and sheet/menu geometry are shared.
items.accessibility: Menu roles, labels, Escape, and restoration are owned by shared overlays.
items.platformNotes: Do not measure anchors or add portal dependencies in a feature.

items.purpose: Own primary, secondary, destructive, loading, selected, focus, hover, and pressed action states.
items.useWhen: An action maps to a button, icon action, link, or selectable row.
items.doNotUseWhen: The interaction needs a new product-neutral semantic owner; propose it first.
items.responsiveBehavior: Supports semantic compact-full action behavior and safe targets.
items.accessibility: Shared roles, labels, pressed state, and keyboard behavior.
items.platformNotes: Never use raw Pressable in feature routes.

items.canonicalName: Card, Avatar, Badge, Tag, Icon, Text
items.purpose: Present standard surfaces, identity, status, iconography, and type with semantic tokens.
items.useWhen: A product needs normal content hierarchy or a status surface.
items.doNotUseWhen: The content is media/image, code, avatar group, or timeline; those are not current shared owners.
items.responsiveBehavior: Consumes shared density and text metrics.
items.accessibility: Text headings and labels use semantic roles.
items.platformNotes: Use @precision-calm/icons rather than direct Lucide imports.

items.purpose: Own responsive primary navigation, contextual tabs, breadcrumbs, and active-state semantics.
items.useWhen: Composing application navigation at a shell or page-context boundary.
items.doNotUseWhen: Implementing route resolution or direct Expo Router calls; use the router adapter.
items.responsiveBehavior: Switches shell presentation without duplicating mounted content.
items.accessibility: Provides named navigation landmarks and tab/pressed semantics.
items.platformNotes: Root shell composition belongs outside ordinary leaf routes.

items.purpose: Isolate Expo Router navigation, protected routes, back fallback, and safe return intent.
items.useWhen: Navigating from a feature or configuring the application root route boundary.
items.doNotUseWhen: Importing expo-router or React Navigation directly in a feature.
items.responsiveBehavior: Pairs with AdaptiveNavigationShell rather than feature viewport logic.
items.accessibility: Shared shell exposes navigation landmarks.
items.platformNotes: The protected-stack integration is root-only.

items.purpose: Present controlled data, search, filters, sorting, selection, bulk actions, and pagination.
items.useWhen: Displaying a moderate structured dataset with product-owned rows and action handlers.
items.doNotUseWhen: The table requires remote cache ownership, 10k-row virtualization, pinning, or column persistence.
items.responsiveBehavior: Transforms to compact records below expanded layouts.
items.accessibility: Selection and rows use shared press/checked semantics.
items.platformNotes: No direct fetch or table-owned query client.

items.purpose: Own list virtualization, sections, refresh, end reach, loading, empty, header, and footer composition.
items.useWhen: Displaying a long or grouped sequence of domain items.
items.doNotUseWhen: A plain small static group can be composed with ListRow, or remote cache behavior is required.
items.responsiveBehavior: Owns one scroll region within shared page geometry.
items.accessibility: List semantics are composed with accessible row owners.
items.platformNotes: Use virtualized ListScreen rather than raw FlatList in feature routes.

items.purpose: Compose semantic entity detail, key/value information, related rows, and metrics.
items.useWhen: Showing an entity or record detail screen.
items.doNotUseWhen: The product requires copy/export/share affordances; those remain incomplete.
items.responsiveBehavior: Detail and master/detail patterns recompose centrally.
items.accessibility: Key/value labels and values preserve structured relationships.
items.platformNotes: Sharing/export is not a current kernel owner.

items.purpose: Add shared live announcements, grouped semantics, and screen-reader-only context.
items.useWhen: A product-specific state change needs an explicit accessible announcement beyond an existing owner.
items.doNotUseWhen: A form, feedback, navigation, or overlay owner already provides the required semantics.
items.responsiveBehavior: No visual geometry ownership is exposed to routes.
items.accessibility: Primary purpose is screen-reader semantics.
items.platformNotes: Use sparingly; do not duplicate announcements.

items.purpose: Own deterministic scoped query identity, request deduplication, cache lifetime, stale state, retries, cancellation, and late-response safety.
items.useWhen: A route reads remote or asynchronous authoritative data through a product service adapter.
items.doNotUseWhen: The work is one isolated user action with no cached server state; use usePrecisionAsyncAction.
items.responsiveBehavior: Not visual; map lifecycle into shared feedback/list/data owners.
items.accessibility: The lifecycle union maps to shared loading/error/degraded announcements rather than route-local spinners.
items.platformNotes: Transport-neutral and React Native/web safe; refocus/reconnect integration remains a Phase 4 root capability.

items.purpose: Refresh one query, invalidate a query or family, cancel work, and update cached data without exposing implementation internals.
items.useWhen: Product logic knows cached data is stale or a successful domain action affects related query identities.
items.doNotUseWhen: A component merely wants to re-render local state or reach into a third-party QueryClient.
items.responsiveBehavior: Not visual.
items.accessibility: Retains usable content during refresh so actions and reading context do not disappear.
items.platformNotes: Persistence and connectivity orchestration are intentionally not enabled.

items.purpose: Own structured mutation outcomes, bounded retries, cache invalidation, late-commit suppression, and deliberate concurrency.
items.useWhen: A user action changes authoritative server data or must coordinate query cache state.
items.doNotUseWhen: The action has no query/cache effects; use usePrecisionAsyncAction for the smaller lifecycle.
items.responsiveBehavior: Pair pending state with shared Button and feedback owners.
items.accessibility: Shared action controls expose busy/disabled semantics while product copy describes the result.
items.platformNotes: Mutations do not retry or persist by default and do not fake offline queuing.

items.purpose: Snapshot, apply, commit, rollback, and invalidate product-approved optimistic changes.
items.useWhen: A domain mutation is safe to represent immediately and has a deterministic rollback.
items.doNotUseWhen: The domain cannot safely predict success, or concurrent optimistic writes have ambiguous ordering.
items.responsiveBehavior: Not visual; existing content remains mounted.
items.accessibility: Products should announce consequential failure/success through shared feedback without removing current context.
items.platformNotes: Parallel optimistic mutations are rejected; choose queue, replace, or single-flight.

items.purpose: Map query lifecycle to initial loading/error/empty and retained-content refreshing/error presentation.
items.useWhen: Rendering a query through shared feedback anatomy while keeping business wording product-owned.
items.doNotUseWhen: The state is a mutation-only action; use Button loading and mutation outcome feedback.
items.responsiveBehavior: Delegates geometry to AsyncStateView and the selected list/data owner.
items.accessibility: Shared feedback owns loading/error/degraded semantics while retained content remains readable and actionable.
items.platformNotes: Offline presentation requires a real future connectivity owner; no offline state is inferred here.

items.purpose: Own isolated user-triggered action state, single-flight behavior, reset, and late-completion protection.
items.useWhen: Submitting, saving, deleting, or retrying one action through an injected service.
items.doNotUseWhen: Managing server-state queries, caching, invalidation, optimistic updates, or offline persistence.
items.responsiveBehavior: Pair state with Button loading and shared feedback components.
items.accessibility: Use semantic action loading/feedback owners for announcements.
items.platformNotes: Does not cancel requests or provide a query cache.

items.purpose: Keep backend/service composition at the root and expose typed product services through runtime context.
items.useWhen: A route needs an approved backend-neutral adapter or service action.
items.doNotUseWhen: Calling fetch, a vendor client, storage, or device API directly in a route.
items.responsiveBehavior: Not visual.
items.accessibility: Pair service outcomes with feedback owners.
items.platformNotes: Optional Expo capability adapters are not installed yet; do not invent a direct boundary.

items.purpose: Use fail-closed auth state and protected routing without feature-owned adapter calls.
items.useWhen: Showing auth state, signing in/out, or configuring protected routes at the root.
items.doNotUseWhen: Implementing provider-specific enrollment, OAuth, recovery, MFA, or backend authorization policy.
items.responsiveBehavior: Pairs with the shared navigation shell.
items.accessibility: Auth routes use standard form/feedback semantics.
items.platformNotes: Provider SDKs remain product-specific.

items.purpose: Evaluate product capabilities from the centralized authorization runtime.
items.useWhen: Conditionally revealing an action or route after auth is ready.
items.doNotUseWhen: Hardcoding roles or assuming client checks replace backend enforcement.
items.responsiveBehavior: Not visual.
items.accessibility: Use clear fallback content for unavailable actions.
items.platformNotes: Backend authorization remains product-owned.

items.purpose: Hold protected navigation until a root-composed session-security adapter resolves.
items.useWhen: Configuring or consuming local session lock state.
items.doNotUseWhen: Calling biometrics or secure storage directly in a feature route.
items.responsiveBehavior: Not visual.
items.accessibility: Use standard unlock form/feedback patterns.
items.platformNotes: Only the memory adapter exists; device-backed adapters are later optional capabilities.

items.purpose: Centralize safe external links, incoming route normalization, and return-intent capture.
items.useWhen: Configuring external/incoming linking at the application integration boundary.
items.doNotUseWhen: Using raw Linking or accepting unvalidated URLs in a feature route.
items.responsiveBehavior: Not visual.
items.accessibility: Use Link for visible link interaction.
items.platformNotes: Expo adapter belongs in root linking composition.

items.purpose: Register explicitly selected capability adapters once without adding native implementations to the kernel.
items.useWhen: An application opts into one or more supported device/browser capabilities.
items.doNotUseWhen: A product is adding a backend vendor, remote-config vendor, or domain service; keep those integrations product-owned.
items.responsiveBehavior: Not visual.
items.accessibility: Capability UI still uses shared feedback and form/overlay owners.
items.platformNotes: The pure kernel package carries contracts only; native implementations are selected separately.

items.purpose: Store secrets through an explicit namespaced SecureStore boundary with a test memory implementation.
items.useWhen: A root-composed session/auth or product integration needs device secret persistence.
items.doNotUseWhen: Saving theme, locale, density, or ordinary preferences; use preferences instead.
items.responsiveBehavior: Not visual.
items.accessibility: Pair storage outcomes with shared feedback; do not expose secret values.
items.platformNotes: Web is explicitly unsupported and never silently falls back to browser storage.

items.purpose: Store non-secret, versioned device-local preferences through one adapter.
items.useWhen: Persisting a local theme, density, locale, or product preference that is not a server-synced setting.
items.doNotUseWhen: Persisting secrets, authorization state, or product domain records.
items.responsiveBehavior: Not visual.
items.accessibility: Preference changes should use shared controls and feedback.
items.platformNotes: Uses browser storage only for ordinary web preferences and AsyncStorage on native.

items.purpose: Normalize connectivity and lifecycle subscriptions and optionally invalidate active server-state queries on real reconnect/foreground transitions.
items.useWhen: A product needs an honest online/offline signal or consciously chooses reconnect/foreground refresh policy.
items.doNotUseWhen: Building offline synchronization, persisted cache, or a route-local AppState listener.
items.responsiveBehavior: Not visual; map state into shared feedback semantics.
items.accessibility: Products own degraded/offline copy; shared feedback owns presentation.
items.platformNotes: Refetch-on-reconnect and foreground are both false by default; no offline queue is implied.

items.purpose: Own capability availability and normalized copy/share outcomes without direct Expo imports in routes.
items.useWhen: Copying a meaningful value or invoking an OS/browser share sheet.
items.doNotUseWhen: Exporting a generated document or implementing product-specific sharing metadata/backend URLs.
items.responsiveBehavior: Not visual.
items.accessibility: Use named Button/Link controls and shared success/error feedback.
items.platformNotes: Availability is checked before sharing; browser support is explicit.

items.purpose: Acquire documents, library media, and camera media with normalized metadata and permission states.
items.useWhen: A product needs user-selected input before its own upload/storage workflow.
items.doNotUseWhen: Rendering media, uploading to a backend, or inventing a feature-local permission lifecycle.
items.responsiveBehavior: Acquisition only; media presentation remains a later visual owner.
items.accessibility: Product rationale copy and selection feedback use shared form/feedback owners.
items.platformNotes: Platform picker behavior is preserved rather than falsely unified; resource metadata is normalized.

items.purpose: Expose enrolled local-device authentication and a root session-security bridge with normalized outcomes.
items.useWhen: Unlocking a locally protected session or approving a local protected action.
items.doNotUseWhen: Authenticating with a backend, authorizing a server request, or replacing product auth enrollment.
items.responsiveBehavior: Not visual.
items.accessibility: Use the shared unlock/feedback workflow; never rely on a biometric prompt as the only explanation.
items.platformNotes: Web is explicitly unsupported by this owner; biometric approval is local-device assurance only.

items.purpose: Own notification permission, explicit token acquisition, and opened-notification events.
items.useWhen: A product has deliberately selected a push backend and needs the device capability boundary.
items.doNotUseWhen: Implementing campaign logic, provider credentials, backend token registration, or business routing.
items.responsiveBehavior: Not visual.
items.accessibility: Products own notification meaning; route visible outcomes through shared feedback.
items.platformNotes: No automatic token registration; web push token support is intentionally unclaimed.

items.purpose: Expose manual update check/download/reload operations without imposing a release policy.
items.useWhen: A product has an approved Expo Updates deployment policy and wants a user-controlled update flow.
items.doNotUseWhen: Configuring update channels, runtime versions, credentials, or automatic production OTA behavior.
items.responsiveBehavior: Not visual.
items.accessibility: Use shared feedback and destructive/restart confirmation patterns where appropriate.
items.platformNotes: Web is unsupported and disabled Expo Updates is configuration-missing; no automatic reload occurs.

items.purpose: Read privacy-safe app version/build, platform, physical-device, and device-class facts.
items.useWhen: Showing product support/version information or adapting a documented capability boundary.
items.doNotUseWhen: Fingerprinting users or adding arbitrary device-specific feature branches.
items.responsiveBehavior: Do not use device class for layout; use shared responsive owners.
items.accessibility: Not visual.
items.platformNotes: No device name, installation identifier, or fingerprinting surface is exposed.

items.purpose: Perform semantic progressive haptic intents through an opt-in capability package.
items.useWhen: A non-essential interaction should offer tactile confirmation on supported hardware.
items.doNotUseWhen: A workflow outcome depends on vibration or a route would import expo-haptics directly.
items.responsiveBehavior: Not visual.
items.accessibility: Haptics supplement, never replace, visible and screen-reader feedback.
items.platformNotes: Web is unsupported; haptic delivery never changes product action success.

items.purpose: Offer a provider-neutral, privacy-aware seam for logs, explicit reports, analytics events, and timing.
items.useWhen: A product has selected a root vendor integration or needs deterministic no-op/recording behavior in tests.
items.doNotUseWhen: Adding a vendor SDK to a feature, silently swallowing errors, or transmitting secrets/PII.
items.responsiveBehavior: Not visual.
items.accessibility: Observability never replaces user-facing shared feedback.
items.platformNotes: No vendor dependency, telemetry, or collection is enabled by default.

items.purpose: Present the supported lightweight chart set with theme-aware responsive geometry and shared data fallback.
items.useWhen: A product needs line, area, bar, donut, sparkline, or progress presentation.
items.doNotUseWhen: It needs stacked/composite analytics, dense marks, sophisticated axes/tooltips, or a full chart engine.
items.responsiveBehavior: Chart solvers adapt to available shared layout width.
items.accessibility: Charts include summaries and can expose a visible keyboard-readable data table.
items.platformNotes: Keep specialized/heavy chart engines optional.

items.purpose: Display determinate progress with shared metrics and native progress semantics.
items.useWhen: Showing known completion or quota progress.
items.doNotUseWhen: Showing indeterminate activity; use LoadingState.
items.responsiveBehavior: Uses shared compact and standard metrics.
items.accessibility: Exposes progress semantics.
items.platformNotes: Portable across supported targets.

items.canonicalName: FormWorkspaceLayout, ReviewWorkflowLayout, ImportWorkflowLayout, CompletionLayout, PermissionRationaleLayout, OfflineWorkspaceLayout
items.purpose: Own canonical multi-section form, review, import, completion, permission, and offline workflow hierarchy without feature-local safe-area, sticky-action, or feedback anatomy.
items.useWhen: A Golden workflow taxonomy entry matches the product request.
items.doNotUseWhen: The workflow is a unique product visualization or domain-specific interaction that has no repeated generic structure.
items.responsiveBehavior: Shared FormScreen, StickyActionBar, Page, and Section owners recompose actions and maintain safe-area ownership.
items.accessibility: Preserves page headings, form error summary placement, toolbar semantics, and shared action order.
items.platformNotes: Optional capabilities remain root-selected; patterns never import Expo device modules.

items.purpose: Map Precision query lifecycle to shared initial loading, stale refresh, error, retry, and empty state anatomy.
items.useWhen: Rendering a query-backed Golden pattern while product code supplies domain copy and content slots.
items.doNotUseWhen: Rendering a purely local action or inventing a route-local query-state switch.
items.responsiveBehavior: Delegates geometry to the enclosing pattern.
items.accessibility: Delegates live/loading/error semantics to AsyncStateView and StateView.
items.platformNotes: Uses @precision-calm/server-state only; no transport, offline queue, or persistence assumptions.

items.purpose: Provide a controlled searchable command dialog with keyboard shortcut, focus lifecycle, disabled commands, and mobile-safe overlay presentation.
items.useWhen: A navigation shell or workflow needs a bounded local command set.
items.doNotUseWhen: Creating a global command bus, a backend search system, or a product-local overlay implementation.
items.responsiveBehavior: Uses the shared dialog on every regime rather than a desktop-only surface.
items.accessibility: Dialog focus trap/restoration, named search input, and list semantics are shared.
items.platformNotes: Command or Control shortcut is used when the host exposes keyboard events; touch users open the controlled dialog through a normal action.

items.purpose: Create a collision-safe Golden route, domain service/model TODO boundary, protected/public route registration, and pattern-owned structure.
items.useWhen: Adding a standard product screen whose Golden workflow has scaffold availability.
items.doNotUseWhen: Overwriting an existing route, creating a trivial component, or forcing a unique product workflow into an unsuitable pattern.
items.responsiveBehavior: Generated routes use pattern-owned adaptive layout; no feature breakpoint logic is emitted.
items.accessibility: Generated composition uses shared semantic owners rather than empty accessibility boilerplate.
items.platformNotes: Capability-aware patterns require an already selected generator capability profile; the scaffold installs nothing.

items.purpose: Own optional expansion, finite single choice, and workflow progress without route-local press/focus/selected mechanics.
items.useWhen: A product needs supplementary inline content, a small finite choice, or to communicate an existing workflow step.
items.doNotUseWhen: Information is critical but hidden behind a tooltip, choices are numerous/searchable, or a route needs domain workflow validation.
items.responsiveBehavior: Uses shared minimum targets and wrapping labels instead of feature breakpoints.
items.accessibility: Disclosure owns expanded state; segmented choices use radio semantics; steps expose progressbar position.
items.platformNotes: No decorative expansion animation is required, so reduced motion remains correct by default.

items.canonicalName: EmailField, UrlField, PhoneField, NumberField, CurrencyField, NumberStepper
items.purpose: Own input intent, labels/errors, locale-aware decimal parsing, blur-only currency formatting, and bounded numeric adjustment.
items.useWhen: Collecting a common email, URL, phone, numeric, currency, or bounded number value.
items.doNotUseWhen: A product needs regional phone policy, accounting rules, date/time/range values, slider gestures, or domain-only parsing; use the date/time owner for portable calendar values.
items.responsiveBehavior: Shared field metrics preserve target safety and allow labels/errors to wrap.
items.accessibility: Uses visible labels, error relationships, keyboard intent, and adjustable stepper semantics.
items.platformNotes: Locale formatting uses the runtime i18n provider; currency is never reformatted mid-entry.

items.purpose: Own searchable popup choice, selected state, keyboard navigation, empty/loading/error feedback, and multi-value toggling.
items.useWhen: Selecting from a bounded or product-filtered option list without rebuilding a Popover and menu in each route.
items.doNotUseWhen: The result set is unbounded, needs a domain search screen, or product code is trying to put a query cache in the field.
items.responsiveBehavior: Uses the collision-aware shared Popover and long-label field anatomy.
items.accessibility: Named combobox/menu semantics, expanded state, selected state, live status, Escape dismissal, and focus restoration are shared.
items.platformNotes: Products connect async options through server-state or a service; the field never owns transport/cache identity.

items.purpose: Unify finite selection group/error semantics instead of multiplying Chip and raw Switch variants.
items.useWhen: A form collects one or more bounded choices, including an error or required state.
items.doNotUseWhen: Choices require search or are a repeatable domain record array.
items.responsiveBehavior: Selection rows keep safe targets and wrap supporting copy at compact widths.
items.accessibility: Checkbox group, radio group, switch, selected, required, and invalid semantics are owner-controlled.
items.platformNotes: Switch rendering remains native while its label/error relationship is shared.

items.purpose: Own provider-neutral OTP/PIN paste, sequential focus, numeric keyboard intent, masking, error, and disabled behavior.
items.useWhen: A product collects a short verification code or local PIN.
items.doNotUseWhen: Implementing MFA/provider enrollment, backend authentication, or a long secret/password.
items.responsiveBehavior: Four-to-eight cells share available width while retaining touch-safe entry geometry.
items.accessibility: Every cell has ordered label text and the enclosing FormField owns error/description semantics.
items.platformNotes: Uses one-time-code hints where the platform exposes them; actual MFA is product-owned.

items.purpose: Add opt-in RHF repeatable fields, hidden-value policy, abortable revision-safe validation, and explicit-cadence autosave without a second form framework.
items.useWhen: A product using RHF needs repeatable typed rows, dependent field reset policy, async server validation, or a consciously chosen autosave cadence.
items.doNotUseWhen: Trying to intercept unsupported router navigation universally, persist drafts without selecting storage, or create a no-policy form DSL.
items.responsiveBehavior: Composes existing FormSection, FormRow, and FormWorkspace owners.
items.accessibility: Retains the shared error summary, field error, focus, and dirty-discard lifecycle.
items.platformNotes: Autosave persistence/upload targets remain product services; durable local drafts require a selected capability.

items.purpose: Own page/cursor/infinite controls and controlled table visibility while existing list owners retain virtualization and refresh.
items.useWhen: A query-backed workspace has page, cursor, or next-page lifecycle, or a moderate table needs user-controlled visible columns.
items.doNotUseWhen: A product needs an enterprise grid with pinning/resizing or assumes a table can virtualize inside an arbitrary scroll surface.
items.responsiveBehavior: Tables preserve compact record transformation; large item sets use the existing virtual list owner.
items.accessibility: Pagination and filter actions are named controls; table selection remains shared.
items.platformNotes: Server-state owns cursors, cached pages, stale data, and refetch—not the data UI.

items.purpose: Own the dense filter overlay trigger, focus lifecycle, apply/clear actions, and compact-safe action hierarchy.
items.useWhen: A browse/data workspace has more filters than quiet inline chips can communicate.
items.doNotUseWhen: A small static filter set fits DataToolbar chips or a domain-specific search route is clearer.
items.responsiveBehavior: Uses shared BottomSheet bounds and stacking on compact and wide screens.
items.accessibility: Shared modal/focus/escape/scroll behavior protects filter fields and actions.
items.platformNotes: Filter parameter/query ownership remains product and server-state code.

items.purpose: Install the shared web focus-visible and forced-colors policy at the document root.
items.useWhen: Composing an Expo Router web document root; generated applications include it automatically.
items.doNotUseWhen: Styling a feature or replacing semantic selected/error state with color alone.
items.responsiveBehavior: Independent of layout and viewport geometry.
items.accessibility: Preserves visible system focus and non-color state boundaries under Windows forced-colors modes.
items.platformNotes: Web document owner only; native accessibility remains source-contracted and runtime-validated separately.

items.purpose: Own responsive aspect ratio, image fit, geometry-preserving loading/error/empty fallback, and alternative text.
items.useWhen: Presenting a local or provider-resolved image/media preview in a product surface.
items.doNotUseWhen: Acquiring camera/library media, uploading, editing media, or using an unreviewed raw Image in a route.
items.responsiveBehavior: Aspect ratio reserves geometry and width follows its shared container.
items.accessibility: Requires meaningful alt text unless explicitly decorative; status fallback is politely announced.
items.platformNotes: No optional picker/camera module is imported; resolve provider URLs outside the visual owner.

items.canonicalName: ChartFrame, LineChart, BarChart, DonutChart, ChartLegend, ChartDataTable
items.purpose: Own lightweight responsive chart framing, loading/error/empty states, categorical donut, legends, selected-point interaction, and optional visible data fallback.
items.useWhen: A product needs a small line, area, bar, donut, trend, or progress visualization with shared state/accessibility anatomy.
items.doNotUseWhen: A product needs stacked/composite analytics, thousands of marks, an enterprise chart engine, or domain-specific visual storytelling.
items.responsiveBehavior: Frame measures available shared width with bounded token heights.
items.accessibility: Noninteractive charts announce a summary; optional ChartDataTable supplies a visible detailed fallback; interactive points are named controls.
items.platformNotes: No decorative animation is required, so reduced-motion behavior is stable without a chart animation engine.

items.purpose: Own image/initial fallback, aggregate avatar overlap, and named non-color status presentation.
items.useWhen: Showing a person or small identity set, or a generic operational status with optional explanation.
items.doNotUseWhen: Encoding product presence rules, domain status taxonomies, or social behavior.
items.responsiveBehavior: Uses semantic size scales, logical overlap, wrapping descriptions, and bounded media geometry.
items.accessibility: Avatars require a name unless decorative; groups have one aggregate name; status always includes visible text.
items.platformNotes: Avatar media delegates to MediaFrame; no acquisition dependency enters the component package.

items.purpose: Present selectable preformatted content with tokenized monospace typography, wrapping or bounded horizontal scroll, and an action slot.
items.useWhen: Showing identifiers, JSON, configuration, logs, or code without syntax-highlighting requirements.
items.doNotUseWhen: Building an editor, terminal, or syntax-highlighting IDE surface.
items.responsiveBehavior: Remains container-bounded; products explicitly choose wrapping versus horizontal scroll.
items.accessibility: Requires a descriptive label and keeps the text selectable; copy is an optional capability-owned action.
items.platformNotes: Uses the platform monospace family without adding a font or highlighting dependency.

items.purpose: Own full, inset, horizontal, and vertical separators through semantic stroke/color tokens.
items.useWhen: Sibling content needs a visible structural separator not already supplied by its shared row/card owner.
items.doNotUseWhen: Spacing or a containing surface communicates grouping more clearly.
items.responsiveBehavior: Logical insets adapt to RTL and remain tokenized across densities.
items.accessibility: Decorative separators are excluded from the accessibility tree.
items.platformNotes: Portable native/web view geometry.

items.purpose: Own capability-backed copy lifecycle, confirmation, failure, truncation, and explicit sensitive-value reveal policy.
items.useWhen: A selected sharing profile needs copyable identifiers, addresses, URLs, code, or explicitly revealable values.
items.doNotUseWhen: Copy is prohibited by product security policy or the value itself should never be rendered.
items.responsiveBehavior: Value truncation and compact actions stay bounded at narrow widths.
items.accessibility: Actions have changing names and polite result feedback; hidden sensitive values are announced as hidden.
items.platformNotes: Use @precision-calm/sharing/ui after selecting the clipboard capability and @precision-calm/sharing/runtime during root registration; there is no direct browser clipboard fallback.

items.purpose: Own portable calendar-date, wall-clock, and ordered-range presentation with explicit transport shapes and locale previews.
items.useWhen: A form can accept explicit YYYY-MM-DD or HH:mm values, or an optional native picker adapter supplies the same values.
items.doNotUseWhen: The product needs scheduling rules, recurrence, timezone conversion, or a bespoke booking calendar.
items.responsiveBehavior: Date ranges stack on compact widths and share field target/error geometry.
items.accessibility: Every value has a visible label, format/locale help, and shared error relationship.
items.platformNotes: Calendar dates and wall-clock values are timezone-free. Native picker UI is an optional documented adapter, not a kernel dependency.

items.purpose: Present ordered chronological events with a shared marker, connector, timestamp, metadata, status, and action anatomy.
items.useWhen: Showing audit history, workflow progress, account activity, order events, or system changes.
items.doNotUseWhen: A general feed/list is more accurate or the domain needs a specialized process diagram.
items.responsiveBehavior: Logical rail placement, compact density, and wrapping event content support RTL and narrow layouts.
items.accessibility: Exposes a named ordered reading sequence; status tone is never the only item information.
items.platformNotes: Portable native/web presentation with product-owned timestamps and ordering.

items.purpose: Serialize product-selected tabular rows deterministically for CSV/tab-delimited copy, download, or sharing recipes.
items.useWhen: A product has already authorized an export and needs neutral tabular serialization.
items.doNotUseWhen: Generating Excel/PDF, defining export permissions, or deciding file delivery and retention policy.
items.responsiveBehavior: Pure data utility; presentation uses data and sharing owners.
items.accessibility: Pair with a named copy/share action and explicit result feedback.
items.platformNotes: No filesystem or sharing dependency; products choose browser download or an optional capability.

items.purpose: Extend the bounded chart set with area emphasis, six-series stacked composition, compact trends, legends, and visible multi-series fallback data.
items.useWhen: A dashboard or report needs an ordinary trend, compact sparkline, or small non-negative stacked composition.
items.doNotUseWhen: A product needs thousands of marks, specialized financial/geographic charts, arbitrary composites, or a general chart engine.
items.responsiveBehavior: Shares ChartFrame measurement, bounded semantic heights, and the six-color visualization palette.
items.accessibility: Charts announce a summary and support a visible data table; stacked categories can expose named touch/keyboard targets.
items.platformNotes: Dependency-free beyond the existing react-native-svg chart boundary; stacked values are finite and non-negative.
